findings.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener (this same PR) invokes clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent when the feature is enabled, and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns the V2 instance. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, deleting any client in any realm fires ClientRemovedEvent, the listener calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...), which throws UnsupportedOperationException, so client deletion fails with a 500 instead of cleaning up (or no-oping) permissions.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 declares a Logger it never uses and carries dead members: getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken), plus imports used only by it (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, AccessToken, EvaluationContext) and the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE. These are leftover scaffolding for the token-exchange override that was replaced by 'throw UnsupportedOperationException'; the next maintainer reading the class must parse ~40 lines of unreachable code to understand what V2 actually supports. Deletion test: removing getEvaluationContext and its imports deletes ~40 lines with zero behavioral change.

[ADVISORY] The @AfterEach in PermissionClientTest deletes scope permissions but never restores the mutating side effects of the test bodies (testManageOnlyOneClient renames myclient to "somethingNew" and removes a default client scope; testManageAllClients creates and deletes a client named "newClient"), and policy cleanup is deferred to realm.cleanup() which runs at realm teardown, not per test. Tests in this class share one managed realm, so later tests operate on a myclient whose name and default client scopes were altered by whichever mutation test ran first; a future test (or a reordering of methods) that asserts on myclient's name, secret, or default scope list fails depending on JUnit method order.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 does not override getAccess(ClientModel), so it inherits the V1 ClientPermissions implementation which is built on the policy/resource methods this class explicitly makes throw UnsupportedOperationException. When V2 is active, the admin console's client 'access' panel (AdminConsoleClientResource / ClientsResource calls permissions.clients().getAccess(client)) hits exchangeToPermission-style V1 internals and throws UnsupportedOperationException, surfacing as a 500 instead of an access map — the client detail page's manage/view/configure buttons break for every admin, not just restricted ones.

[BUG] canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission are stubbed with 'throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")' with no V2-equivalent implementation and no test anywhere in the diff exercising the token-exchange path under V2. With admin fine-grained authz V2 enabled, any configured token-exchange flow that consults client exchange permissions crashes with UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500) instead of a permission decision — a silently dropped requirement; no section of the PR documents that token exchange is intentionally unsupported, and the private getEvaluationContext/ClientModelIdentity machinery at lines 263-275 shows the author intended to implement it but shipped the stub.

[ADVISORY] The new canMapClientScopeRoles path (AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE) has no test coverage: PermissionClientTest imports and exercises MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE (testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient) but no assertion in the diff ever grants or denies the map-roles-client-scope scope. A regression in canMapClientScopeRoles (e.g. wrong scope string or a missing admin-role fallback, which this method conspicuously lacks compared to canManage/canView) would pass the entire test suite; administrators granting client-scope role-mapping rights get silently denied (or granted) with no test failing.

[ADVISORY] The RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup listener is now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), whereas previously it ran unconditionally. An operator who enables fine-grained admin authz, creates per-object policies, then disables the feature leaves orphaned authorization resources/policies in the store permanently — the cleanup listener no longer fires on object removal once the feature is off, and nothing in the diff removes the stale data at disable time. Who gets bitten: anyone toggling the feature off in a realm that used it.

[ADVISORY] The static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE and the private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) method are dead code shipped in this diff — no call site in the class reaches either once canExchangeTo was stubbed to throw. The next reader reasonably concludes token-exchange evaluation is wired up (imports and context builder present) when it is not; the dead method also references the identity/attribute plumbing that will drift from real usage. Deletion test passes: removing both the import and getEvaluationContext deletes ~15 lines with zero behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The permission-granted-checking loop is copy-pasted three times (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) ~lines 225-239, hasPermission(String) ~lines 250-265, hasGrantedPermission ~lines 278-285) with already-diverging mechanics (Arrays.asList+contains vs direct String.equals). The next scope added to the Clients resource type requires touching three near-identical loops; the observed drift (equals vs contains) is the classic seed of a future inconsistency where one path matches scopes case-insensitively or via a different set semantics. Extraction to a single hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope) helper deletes ~25 lines and removes the drift.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 stubs out fourteen inherited ClientPermissions methods (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) with UnsupportedOperationException, but these methods are called by existing admin REST endpoints and by the AdminPermissions event listener registered in this same PR. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ V2 active, any admin operation that touches token-exchange grants, per-client permission management UI endpoints (ClientsResource permission endpoints), or the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup path (AdminPermissions.java now calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)) throws UnsupportedOperationException and surfaces as a 500 instead of the documented behavior — an existing, working admin API surface is broken by this change rather than extended.

[ADVISORY] Gating the entire RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup listener behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) is unrelated to the PR's stated intent of adding the Client resource type, and changes behavior for realms where the feature is disabled at the time a removal event fires. If a realm previously had the feature enabled (fine-grained authz resources created), then the profile is disabled and a role/client/group is removed, the orphaned authorization resources are no longer cleaned up because the listener now no-ops — stale resources accumulate. Also, evaluating the profile flag on every provider event for all realms adds a behavior change not traceable to any requirement in this PR; it should either be a separate change or justified in the PR description.

[ADVISORY] The private helper getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token) is dead code: its only plausible caller, canExchangeTo, is stubbed with UnsupportedOperationException in the same file. Fails the deletion test — removing getEvaluationContext (and the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/AccessToken imports it alone pulls in) deletes ~11 lines with no behavior change; leaving it misleads future readers into thinking V2 token-exchange evaluation is implemented when it is not.

[ADVISORY] testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient exercises MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE but never exercises the new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope, even though AdminPermissionsSchema.ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles is new non-trivial logic introduced by this diff. A regression in canMapClientScopeRoles (e.g. scope name typo or missing scope on the CLIENTS ResourceType) ships undetected; any admin flow that manages client-scope role mappings (RoleMapperResource client-level role mapping for scopes) would silently 403 for users granted that scope, and no test in the diff would fail.

[ADVISORY] canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles in V2 drop the admin-role short-circuit that all other V2 overrides retain (no root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) check), diverging from both the documented contract in ClientPermissionEvaluator.canMapRoles javadoc ('For V2 only: Also if...') and the pattern used by canManage/canView/canManageClientScopes in this same class. An admin holding the MANAGE_CLIENTS realm role but granted no explicit map-roles permission is denied role-mapping operations under V2 while being allowed every other manage operation, producing an inconsistent permission surface that the updated interface docs do not describe; the next person editing V2 must know this asymmetry to avoid breaking it.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled, but AdminPermissions.registerListener routes ClientRemovedEvent directly into that method, so client deletion fails under V2. When the V2 permission management is active, deleting any client (or any group/role, via the sibling events in the same listener) triggers AdminPermissions.registerListener's call to management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which hits the V2 override and throws UnsupportedOperationException, turning a routine client deletion into a 500 and leaving the admin console unable to remove clients.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 leaves canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, resource, getPermissions and isPermissionsEnabled as UnsupportedOperationException while the class is wired in as the clients() implementation for the whole admin surface. Every existing caller of the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface outside this diff — the admin REST endpoints for per-client permission management (ClientsResource permission views), token-exchange authorization (canExchangeTo is on the hot path of the token exchange grant), and any code reading isPermissionsEnabled — now gets an UnsupportedOperationException/500 under V2 with no versioning or deprecation path; these are advertised interface methods with no working implementation behind them.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission iterates every Clients-typed resource in the store and runs a full policy-engine evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) per resource, an O(n) evaluation fan-out on the admin client-listing hot path. Every realm-client list/search call in a realm with per-client permissions pays one complete authorization policy evaluation per registered client resource (and the callback-driven findByType materializes all of them), so a realm with thousands of clients sees a wall of policy evaluations per request; an indexed pre-filter or batched evaluation keyed on the granted policy would avoid the cliff.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel, String) calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) — a get-or-create — on a pure permission-evaluation read path, before checking whether any policies exist, so evaluating permissions for a client with no per-client resource writes the 'Clients' type resource into the authorization store as a side effect. A read-only permission check (e.g., every admin request against a client that has no explicit permission) mutates the resource store on first miss; besides the write-on-read surprise, concurrent requests can race on the create and the resource is created even when the immediately-following empty-policy check would have made it useless.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 declares an unused Logger, imports TOKEN_EXCHANGE, and carries a private getEvaluationContext helper whose only conceivable consumer (canExchangeTo) throws UnsupportedOperationException — all dead code shipped in this diff. The dead evaluation-context builder implies exchange evaluation is implemented when it is not; the next maintainer wiring token-exchange into V2 will assume this helper is exercised and tested when it has zero call sites. Deleting getEvaluationContext and the unused imports removes ~20 lines and a false affordance.

[BUG] MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() unconditionally returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose canExchangeTo() throws UnsupportedOperationException, silently deleting the token-exchange permission behavior that ClientPermissionsV1 provided for the same realm once ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is active. Any admin token-exchange flow or admin REST endpoint that calls clients().canExchangeTo(...)/exchangeToPermission(...) gets a raw UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500) instead of a permission decision; the PR's stated objective was to add a Clients resource type, not to remove token-exchange grant checks, and no human acceptance of that removal is recorded in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The V2 override set throws UnsupportedOperationException for the whole per-client permission-management surface (setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission), while the PR's stated objective is only to add the Clients resource type and scopes to the schema. Operators on V2 realms can no longer toggle per-client fine-grained permissions or inspect them (admin console 'Permissions' tab on a client), a silent capability removal beyond the declared scope; anyone relying on the V1 per-client permission model is bitten at upgrade time with runtime exceptions rather than a documented contract change.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) changes the authorization semantics for MANAGE: in V1 canManage(client) granted map-roles/composite/client-scope implicitly via manage, but V2's canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles consult only their dedicated scopes, so a caller granted MANAGE on a client silently loses role-mapping abilities it had under the same grant in V1. Administrators with a MANAGE permission on a client who could previously map roles under V1 semantics get 403s after the V2 evaluator is wired in; the new javadoc documents the narrowed rule but the implicit-narrowing of MANAGE's reach is an intent change to the accepted permission model, not an explicitly accepted constraint.

[ADVISORY] The listener refactor adds a Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) gate around the RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent cleanup, changing pre-existing behavior: previously these events always triggered setPermissionsEnabled(false) regardless of the feature flag. In deployments where the admin-fine-grained-authz feature is disabled but legacy authorization resources still exist (e.g., the feature was toggled off after permissions were created), removed roles/clients/groups now leak their stale authz permission resources forever, a behavior change made silently inside a PR whose objective was adding a Clients resource type.

[ADVISORY] The new javadoc for canConfigure/canView/canMapRoles claims the caller is also granted when it has a permission to ClientPermissionManagement#MANAGE_SCOPE, CONFIGURE_SCOPE, or MAP_ROLES_SCOPE 'the client', but ClientPermissionsV2 implements only the global type-level check (hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE) on the per-client/type resource) and never consults the V1 per-client scope objects those constants name, so the documented contract and the shipped behavior have silently diverged. A developer reading the interface contract and granting the V1 per-client CONFIGURE_SCOPE permission expects canConfigure to return true; on V2 realms it returns false because those V1 scope permissions are never evaluated (their accessors throw UnsupportedOperationException), so consumers of the documented API get 403s where the contract promises access.

[BUG] hasPermission(ClientModel, String) never consults the all-clients (Clients-type) permission when a per-client resource already exists, so a type-level grant silently stops applying to any client that has any per-client resource created for it. An admin granted MANAGE/VIEW on all clients (the pattern createAllPermission uses) loses that grant on a specific client the moment any other admin attaches a per-client resource/policy to that client — the previously-authorized caller is denied with ForbiddenException despite the all-clients grant still being in force; V1 semantics union both, so this is a privilege-check asymmetry that bites whoever administers mixed per-client/all-clients permissions.

[BUG] canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions all throw UnsupportedOperationException, so token-exchange authorization in V2 realms raises a runtime exception instead of an authorization decision. Any admin or token-exchange code path in a V2 (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ v2) realm that calls canExchangeTo (token exchange between clients) or setPermissionsEnabled (the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup listener registered in AdminPermissions.registerListener now calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled on every client deletion) throws UnsupportedOperationException, turning client deletion and token exchange into 500 errors; deletion-time cleanup of authorization resources for clients never runs in V2 realms.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission enumerates every Clients-type resource in the realm and runs a full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) for each one on every invocation. On the admin client-list path in a realm with fine-grained client permissions enabled and thousands of clients, each list call performs thousands of policy evaluations against the authz store, producing a hot-path O(n) regression that admins of large realms hit on every clients().findAll(); the result set is also not capped, so the caller receives one evaluation per resource regardless of pagination.

[BUG] The all-clients fallback in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) gates on policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty(), which only finds policies attached directly to the type resource and misses resourceType-based scope permissions (the form the tests create via .resourceType(clientsType)). When the only all-clients permissions are resourceType-scoped (the documented creation path used by PermissionClientTest.createAllPermission), findByResource returns empty and hasPermission returns false without ever evaluating, so authorized admins are denied MANAGE/VIEW on every client lacking a per-client resource — the grant exists, is visible in the admin console, and is silently ignored by the evaluation path.

[ADVISORY] resolveClient accepts either the internal UUID or the client_id string as the resource identifier, so authorization resources for clients can be keyed by two different caller-supplied aliases of the same client. An admin creating a fine-grained permission who passes the client_id string gets a resource whose name is the resolved internal id, while a caller who guesses/uses a different alias against the permission-creation endpoint gets a fresh lookup — combined with getOrCreateResource's create-if-absent path, two resources for the same client could be created by feeding different aliases over time, splitting the permission surface so one grant silently doesn't match the resource the evaluator looks up; anyone scripting permissions against the admin REST API with mixed id/clientId inputs gets inconsistent authorization results.

[ADVISORY] The new canMapClientScopeRoles / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission path has zero test coverage: no test in the diff grants or exercises the map-roles-client-scope scope, so this new authorization branch is verified by nothing. A regression in client-scope role-mapping authorization (e.g. the hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE) lookup never matching, or the wrong scope name wired in) would pass the entire suite; an admin granted only client-scope-role-mapping permission would silently be unable to (or improperly able to) map client-scope roles. Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, AbstractPermissionTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — none reference MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE or call any client-scope role-mapping endpoint. Rebuttal: testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient covers MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE — but it never touches the client-scope variant at all, so it does not cover this branch.

[ADVISORY] The resolveClient fallback branch (looking the client up by clientId when getClientById returns null) is never triggered by any test in the diff — every test passes the internal UUID (myclient.getId()), so the getClientByClientId fallback path and the null-name failure path when the client does not exist are unverified. If the fallback lookup is wrong (e.g. wrong store call, or the name-normalization contract differs from Users where resolveUser returns the id), a client permission created by clientId would silently fail to resolve and permission evaluation would wrongly deny or fall through to the all-clients resource; no test would catch it. Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, AbstractPermissionTest.java — all pass resource ids via .getId(). Rebuttal: id-based lookup covers the primary path — but the fallback branch is explicitly added new logic in this diff, which is exactly what this lens flags.

[ADVISORY] The behavioral change wrapping the entire ProviderEventListener in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) has no test exercising the disabled-feature path — no test in the diff verifies that role/client/group removal still behaves correctly when the feature is off (or that cleanup still fires when it is on). If the feature-flag check is wrong (or the listener registration order means Profile is not yet initialized, always evaluating false), stale authorization resources accumulate after role/client/group removal and no test fails. Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java — none remove a client/role/group to assert the cleanup event path under either feature state. Rebuttal: KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig implies the tests run with the feature enabled — but that means only the enabled branch is exercised and the newly added gate itself is never verified in either direction, and no test deletes a client to confirm setPermissionsEnabled(false) still fires.

[ADVISORY] The thirteen new UnsupportedOperationException overrides (canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, and the Policy factory methods) have no test asserting they throw under V2, nor any test showing the calling endpoints degrade gracefully rather than 500. Any admin-console or admin-client flow that calls e.g. clients().get(id).getPermissionsManager-style endpoints or token-exchange evaluation under V2 will surface an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException as a 500, and no test in this diff pins that behavior (or verifies those endpoints are actually unreachable). Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java — none touch the permission-management endpoints or canExchangeTo for clients. Rebuttal: 'the UI does not call these in V2' is asserted nowhere in the diff, so the contract is unverified.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent, so with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled (the exact condition the new listener gate checks) MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() hands back this V2 instance and client deletion blows up. Deleting any client in a realm while the feature is enabled throws UnsupportedOperationException from the ProviderEventListener, failing or aborting client removal (and leaving the removal half-complete), instead of cleaning up authorization resources as the pre-diff code did.

[BUG] The removal-cleanup listener is now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) evaluated at event time, so a realm that had the feature enabled (creating per-client/role/group permission resources) and is later disabled stops cleaning up those authorization resources on ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent. Orphaned resource/policy rows for removed clients, roles, and groups accumulate permanently in the authorization tables once the flag is turned off, with no code path left that deletes them; also a rolling deploy where some pods run old (ungated) and some new (gated) code produces inconsistent cleanup for the same events.

[BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent cleanup handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which in V2 mode dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — a method that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. When the V2 admin-permissions implementation is active, deleting any client fires ClientRemovedEvent, the listener invokes ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, and the UnsupportedOperationException propagates out of the event listener into the delete flow, failing the client-removal request with a raw 500 instead of completing the delete (or at minimum leaving the delete aborted and stale authz resources behind). The V1 cleanup contract silently regressed because the shared event listener was not updated to the V2 no-op semantics.

[ADVISORY] canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, and getPermissions all throw bare UnsupportedOperationException with no feature-aware guarding or 4xx mapping. Any admin-console flow or admin-client caller that still touches these V1 surface methods (token-exchange permission management, per-client permission resource inspection, enable/disable permissions toggles) gets an unhandled 500 from a permission evaluator that used to return a real result, with an error shape the admin API never promised; callers cannot distinguish 'unsupported in V2' from a server bug.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel, String) calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) — a get-or-create — on a read/authorization-check path when the per-client resource is absent. Every permission evaluation for a client that has no per-client resource materializes the 'Clients' type resource in the authorization store as a side effect of a read; a realm with many clients evaluated by fine-grained admins accumulates created resources on every check, and a read-only/limited store is mutated by a pure canXxx() query — an unexpected write during authorization evaluation.

[ADVISORY] The cleanup listeners for RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, and GroupRemovedEvent are now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), whereas they previously ran unconditionally. If any fine-grained authorization data (role/client/group permission resources and policies) exists in a realm where the feature flag is later disabled, deletion events no longer clean up those authz objects, leaving orphaned resources that silently skew any re-enabled evaluation; also, if the V2 implementation is served under a different feature flag than ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, the cleanup listeners are dead code for V2 realms entirely.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, when Profile.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, a ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent triggers `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). In this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides `clients()` to return a `ClientPermissionsV2` instance (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java). `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` is overridden to unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). Therefore, under the feature flag, processing a ClientRemovedEvent will call a method that throws, likely causing a 500 during client deletion/cleanup instead of disabling/no-oping permissions.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, ClientPermissionEvaluator’s new Javadoc states canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles for a specific client can also be granted via V1-style per-client permissions (e.g., “permission to ClientPermissionManagement#CONFIGURE_SCOPE the client” / “AdminPermissionManagement#MANAGE_SCOPE”). However, the new ClientPermissionsV2 implementation overrides these checks and only evaluates AdminPermissionsSchema scopes via hasPermission(client, ...): canConfigure() -> hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE) (or canManage), canManage() -> hasPermission(client, MANAGE), canMapRoles() -> hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES), etc., and it never consults any V1 per-client scope objects. Additionally, V1-style permission-management methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (e.g., configurePermission/managePermission/mapRolesPermission, isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled) throw UnsupportedOperationException, reinforcing that those V1 mechanisms are not evaluated in V2. This is a verifiable contract/behavior divergence introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] hasPermission(ClientModel, String) never consults the all-clients (Clients-type) permission when a per-client resource already exists, so a type-level grant silently stops applying to any client that has any per-client resource created for it. An admin granted MANAGE/VIEW on all clients (the pattern createAllPermission uses) loses that grant on a specific client the moment any other admin attaches a per-client resource/policy to that client — the previously-authorized caller is denied with ForbiddenException despite the all-clients grant still being in force; V1 semantics union both, so this is a privilege-check asymmetry that bites whoever administers mixed per-client/all-clients permissions.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code evaluates **either** the per-client `Resource` (found by `client.getId()`) **or**, only if that is missing, falls back to the type-level/all-clients resource (`getResourceTypeResource(... CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`). If a per-client resource exists, the method never consults the all-clients/type-level permission, so a type-level grant (created by `createAllPermission(...)`) can be effectively ignored for that client once any per-client resource exists. This contradicts the newly added V2 semantics documented in `ClientPermissionEvaluator` (e.g., `canManage(ClientModel)` / `canConfigure(ClientModel)` “also if ... permission to MANAGE/CONFIGURE all clients”), and can lead to unexpected `ForbiddenException` denials in mixed setups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions all throw UnsupportedOperationException, so token-exchange authorization in V2 realms raises a runtime exception instead of an authorization decision. Any admin or token-exchange code path in a V2 (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ v2) realm that calls canExchangeTo (token exchange between clients) or setPermissionsEnabled (the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup listener registered in AdminPermissions.registerListener now calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled on every client deletion) throws UnsupportedOperationException, turning client deletion and token exchange into 500 errors; deletion-time cleanup of authorization resources for clients never runs in V2 realms.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is overridden to return a new ClientPermissionsV2 (services/.../MgmtPermissionsV2.java). ClientPermissionsV2 overrides multiple methods, including setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) and canExchangeTo(...), to unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). AdminPermissions.registerListener now (when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled) handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). If management(...) returns MgmtPermissionsV2 in the V2 mode, that call will throw at runtime during client deletion, turning cleanup into a 500 and preventing cleanup logic from running. The same pattern applies to any V2 call path that invokes canExchangeTo(...) (token exchange checks) since it also throws rather than returning an authorization decision.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission enumerates every Clients-type resource in the realm and runs a full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) for each one on every invocation. On the admin client-list path in a realm with fine-grained client permissions enabled and thousands of clients, each list call performs thousands of policy evaluations against the authz store, producing a hot-path O(n) regression that admins of large realms hit on every clients().findAll(); the result set is also not capped, so the caller receives one evaluation per resource regardless of pagination.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(String)` (new file), the method iterates over *all* authz resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and for each resource calls `hasGrantedPermission(...)`, which invokes `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))`. This is a per-resource full policy evaluation and the method returns an unbounded `Set` with no pagination/capping. While the diff does not show the call site (`clients().findAll()` path) to prove it’s on the hot list path, the implementation itself is clearly O(n) evaluations over all client resources and is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by this change rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The all-clients fallback in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) gates on policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty(), which only finds policies attached directly to the type resource and misses resourceType-based scope permissions (the form the tests create via .resourceType(clientsType)). When the only all-clients permissions are resourceType-scoped (the documented creation path used by PermissionClientTest.createAllPermission), findByResource returns empty and hasPermission returns false without ever evaluating, so authorized admins are denied MANAGE/VIEW on every client lacking a per-client resource — the grant exists, is visible in the admin console, and is silently ignored by the evaluation path.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no per-client `Resource` exists it falls back to the resource-type resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`) but then short-circuits with `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` (new code in `ClientPermissionsV2`). This check only detects policies directly linked to that specific `Resource`. The tests added/updated in this diff create “all clients” permissions via `createAllPermission(...).resourceType(clientsType)` (no `resources(...)`), i.e., resourceType-based scope permissions, not resource-attached policies. With only those permissions present, `findByResource(...)` can be empty and the method returns `false` without evaluating, incorrectly denying access despite an existing resourceType grant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] resolveClient accepts either the internal UUID or the client_id string as the resource identifier, so authorization resources for clients can be keyed by two different caller-supplied aliases of the same client. An admin creating a fine-grained permission who passes the client_id string gets a resource whose name is the resolved internal id, while a caller who guesses/uses a different alias against the permission-creation endpoint gets a fresh lookup — combined with getOrCreateResource's create-if-absent path, two resources for the same client could be created by feeding different aliases over time, splitting the permission surface so one grant silently doesn't match the resource the evaluator looks up; anyone scripting permissions against the admin REST API with mixed id/clientId inputs gets inconsistent authorization results.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `resolveClient(KeycloakSession, String id)` normalizes both inputs (either internal UUID via `getClientById` or `clientId` via `getClientByClientId`) to a single canonical identifier by returning `client.getId()` in both cases. `getOrCreateResource(...)` then uses this resolved value (`name = resolveClient(...)`) for clients, so different aliases do not result in different resource names and should not create two distinct resources for the same client based on UUID vs `clientId` input. The described “two resources keyed by different caller-supplied aliases” behavior is not supported by what’s shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new canMapClientScopeRoles / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission path has zero test coverage: no test in the diff grants or exercises the map-roles-client-scope scope, so this new authorization branch is verified by nothing. A regression in client-scope role-mapping authorization (e.g. the hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE) lookup never matching, or the wrong scope name wired in) would pass the entire suite; an admin granted only client-scope-role-mapping permission would silently be unable to (or improperly able to) map client-scope roles. Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, AbstractPermissionTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java — none reference MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE or call any client-scope role-mapping endpoint. Rebuttal: testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient covers MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE — but it never touches the client-scope variant at all, so it does not cover this branch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new scope constant and authorization branch for client-scope role mapping: AdminPermissionsSchema adds MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE and includes it in CLIENTS ResourceType scopes, and ClientPermissionsV2 adds canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel) -> hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE). In the modified/added tests (e.g., PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient), permissions granted to the client are only MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, and CONFIGURE, and no test references MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE or exercises a client-scope role-mapping endpoint. Therefore this new scope/branch is not covered by any test shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The resolveClient fallback branch (looking the client up by clientId when getClientById returns null) is never triggered by any test in the diff — every test passes the internal UUID (myclient.getId()), so the getClientByClientId fallback path and the null-name failure path when the client does not exist are unverified. If the fallback lookup is wrong (e.g. wrong store call, or the name-normalization contract differs from Users where resolveUser returns the id), a client permission created by clientId would silently fail to resolve and permission evaluation would wrongly deny or fall through to the all-clients resource; no test would catch it. Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java, AbstractPermissionTest.java — all pass resource ids via .getId(). Rebuttal: id-based lookup covers the primary path — but the fallback branch is explicitly added new logic in this diff, which is exactly what this lens flags.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new resolution logic for client resources in AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient(): first session.clients().getClientById(realm, id), then fallback to session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id), and returns client.getId() or null. In the added/modified tests (notably PermissionClientTest) the permission resources are created using myclient.getId() (UUID) via createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, ...), so the fallback branch (lookup by clientId string) and the name==null path when a client cannot be resolved are not exercised by any test shown in the diff. This is a concrete, diff-grounded coverage gap for newly introduced nontrivial behavior, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The behavioral change wrapping the entire ProviderEventListener in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) has no test exercising the disabled-feature path — no test in the diff verifies that role/client/group removal still behaves correctly when the feature is off (or that cleanup still fires when it is on). If the feature-flag check is wrong (or the listener registration order means Profile is not yet initialized, always evaluating false), stale authorization resources accumulate after role/client/group removal and no test fails. Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java — none remove a client/role/group to assert the cleanup event path under either feature state. Rebuttal: KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig implies the tests run with the feature enabled — but that means only the enabled branch is exercised and the newly added gate itself is never verified in either direction, and no test deletes a client to confirm setPermissionsEnabled(false) still fires.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new feature-flag gate around *all* cleanup handling in `AdminPermissions.registerListener`: `onEvent` now only processes `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` when `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` is true. This is a nontrivial behavioral change (previously cleanup always ran). The added/modified tests in the diff (e.g., `PermissionClientTest`, `PermissionRESTTest`, `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) focus on permission evaluation and CRUD, but none trigger removal events (delete a client/role/group) to assert that the listener cleanup path runs when enabled, nor do they cover the disabled-feature path introduced by the new gate. That makes the review concern diff-grounded and actionable, but not a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The thirteen new UnsupportedOperationException overrides (canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, and the Policy factory methods) have no test asserting they throw under V2, nor any test showing the calling endpoints degrade gracefully rather than 500. Any admin-console or admin-client flow that calls e.g. clients().get(id).getPermissionsManager-style endpoints or token-exchange evaluation under V2 will surface an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException as a 500, and no test in this diff pins that behavior (or verifies those endpoints are actually unreachable). Test files checked: PermissionClientTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java — none touch the permission-management endpoints or canExchangeTo for clients. Rebuttal: 'the UI does not call these in V2' is asserted nowhere in the diff, so the contract is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` with many overridden methods that unconditionally `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, the various `*Permission(...)` factory methods, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). The added/modified tests (`PermissionClientTest`, `PermissionRESTTest`, `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) exercise V2 client CRUD and scope-permission evaluation, but they do not assert these UnsupportedOperationException paths nor demonstrate that any endpoints that might reach them are unreachable/handled. While the claim that this will surface as a 500 in real flows is not verifiable from the diff alone (no calling endpoints shown), the lack of contract/tests around intentionally-unsupported overrides is a concrete, diff-grounded gap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent, so with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled (the exact condition the new listener gate checks) MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() hands back this V2 instance and client deletion blows up. Deleting any client in a realm while the feature is enabled throws UnsupportedOperationException from the ProviderEventListener, failing or aborting client removal (and leaving the removal half-complete), instead of cleaning up authorization resources as the pre-diff code did.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now runs its cleanup logic only when `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` is true, and for `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. The diff also introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning a cached `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` is overridden to throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If `management(...)` resolves to `MgmtPermissionsV2` under this feature (which is strongly implied by adding V2 permissions classes and gating the listener by the same feature), then deleting a client will trigger the listener and throw `UnsupportedOperationException` during the event, breaking the deletion cleanup flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The removal-cleanup listener is now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) evaluated at event time, so a realm that had the feature enabled (creating per-client/role/group permission resources) and is later disabled stops cleaning up those authorization resources on ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent. Orphaned resource/policy rows for removed clients, roles, and groups accumulate permanently in the authorization tables once the flag is turned off, with no code path left that deletes them; also a rolling deploy where some pods run old (ungated) and some new (gated) code produces inconsistent cleanup for the same events.

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the cleanup logic for `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` is now wrapped inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` (see modified `onEvent`). Previously these events always triggered `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`. With this diff, if the feature flag is disabled at event time, the listener performs no cleanup at all for removals, and the diff shows no alternate code path that would remove/disable the corresponding authz artifacts. This makes it verifiable from the diff that cleanup behavior is now dependent on runtime flag state, which can leave previously-created permission resources/policies uncleaned when the flag is off.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent cleanup handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which in V2 mode dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — a method that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. When the V2 admin-permissions implementation is active, deleting any client fires ClientRemovedEvent, the listener invokes ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, and the UnsupportedOperationException propagates out of the event listener into the delete flow, failing the client-removal request with a raw 500 instead of completing the delete (or at minimum leaving the delete aborted and stale authz resources behind). The V1 cleanup contract silently regressed because the shared event listener was not updated to the V2 no-op semantics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a V2 client permissions implementation where `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). The shared admin-permissions event listener (`AdminPermissions.registerListener`) still invokes `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` (now gated by `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`). The same diff also wires V2 management to return `ClientPermissionsV2` via `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()`. If `management(...)` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` under the feature flag, client deletion will trigger the listener and call the throwing method, causing an exception during the delete flow (likely a 500). This is a verifiable incompatibility between the listener cleanup contract and the new V2 behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, managePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, and getPermissions all throw bare UnsupportedOperationException with no feature-aware guarding or 4xx mapping. Any admin-console flow or admin-client caller that still touches these V1 surface methods (token-exchange permission management, per-client permission resource inspection, enable/disable permissions toggles) gets an unhandled 500 from a permission evaluator that used to return a real result, with an error shape the admin API never promised; callers cannot distinguish 'unsupported in V2' from a server bug.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class, multiple overridden methods throw a bare `UnsupportedOperationException`, including `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)` (and `isPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, etc.). The diff also shows `AdminPermissions.registerListener` calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent` (and this logic now runs when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled). With `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returning `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)`, this call path can trigger the `UnsupportedOperationException`, resulting in an unhandled server error instead of a controlled/feature-aware behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel, String) calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) — a get-or-create — on a read/authorization-check path when the per-client resource is absent. Every permission evaluation for a client that has no per-client resource materializes the 'Clients' type resource in the authorization store as a side effect of a read; a realm with many clients evaluated by fine-grained admins accumulates created resources on every check, and a read-only/limited store is mutated by a pure canXxx() query — an unexpected write during authorization evaluation.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when the per-client `Resource` is absent (`resourceStore.findByName(...)` returns null), the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. Unlike the other helper `hasPermission(String)` which uses a pure lookup (`resourceStore.findByName(...)`), this fallback path relies on schema-level resource retrieval that (by naming/usage pattern in this diff, alongside the schema’s explicit `getOrCreateResource(...)` behavior added for CLIENTS) plausibly creates/materializes the type resource during what is otherwise a read-only authorization check. That is a concrete, diff-grounded design/side-effect concern (unexpected writes/perf bloat) even though the exact create-vs-get semantics of `getResourceTypeResource` aren’t shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cleanup listeners for RoleRemovedEvent, ClientRemovedEvent, and GroupRemovedEvent are now gated behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), whereas they previously ran unconditionally. If any fine-grained authorization data (role/client/group permission resources and policies) exists in a realm where the feature flag is later disabled, deletion events no longer clean up those authz objects, leaving orphaned resources that silently skew any re-enabled evaluation; also, if the V2 implementation is served under a different feature flag than ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, the cleanup listeners are dead code for V2 realms entirely.
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: the removal/cleanup listeners are guarded by the V1 feature flag (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which can prevent cleanup when fine-grained authz is active under a different/V2 flag. This leads to orphaned permission/authz objects when V2 is enabled but V1 is not (or when the flag is later disabled), matching the golden issue about inconsistent feature-flag gating causing missed cleanup.
